title: Optional visits, penalties, and pickup and delivery

questions.heading: The Penalty Decides What Gets Dropped
questions.stem: A routing model's arc costs are drive minutes, and all the arcs of its matrix add up to 6,000. The planner wants routine visits dropped only when the crews truly cannot fit them. Which penalty per routine visit matches that policy?

options.text: 10, far below the 6,000 that the matrix's arcs add up to
options.says: A small penalty lets the solver drop a visit just to save driving, as cof // 100 did in the lesson.

options.text: 0, so the 6,000 of driving is all the objective counts
options.says: A penalty of 0 makes a drop free, so the solver drops any visit that costs driving.

options.text: Each visit's drive from the depot, a share of the matrix's 6,000
options.says: That drops a far visit whenever its detour costs more than its drive from the depot, even when it fits.

options.text: 10,000, above the 6,000 that the matrix's arcs add up to
options.says: Right: above the sum of all arc costs, no drop can pay for itself in driving.

questions.heading: A Dropped Visit Is an Index That Points to Itself
questions.stem: A solve with optional visits has finished. How do you tell from the solution that one visit was left off every route?

options.text: Its successor is the end index of the vehicle that would have served it
options.says: A visit that points to an end is the last stop of a route, not a dropped one.

options.text: Its successor variable holds its own index, so it points to itself
options.says: Right: a dropped visit has next_i = i.

options.text: Its successor is the start index of the first vehicle
options.says: A dropped visit is its own successor; a start index is where a vehicle's route begins.

options.text: Its successor is the next visit on the nearest route
options.says: A dropped visit is on no route, so the model makes it its own successor: next_i = i.

questions.heading: Pickup and Delivery Is a Pair, a Same-Vehicle Row and an Order Row
questions.stem: A model calls AddPickupAndDelivery and adds the order row for each pair, but no same-vehicle row. Which hand-built plan did OR-Tools 9.15 accept that no courier could carry out?

options.text: One car reaches the delivery first and the pickup later on its route
options.says: That plan was refused in every version of the model, the declaration alone included.

options.text: One car makes the pickup and then the delivery, in that order
options.says: That plan is accepted, and a courier can carry it out.

options.text: One car makes the pickup and another car makes the delivery
options.says: Right: without the same-vehicle row the split plan was accepted.

options.text: None, since the declaration alone keeps the pair in one car
options.says: The declaration alone accepted the split plan; only the same-vehicle row refused it.
